inputs.content:
# Brightwork: should we launch an AI dispatch assistant? — briefing pack

> **Synthetic benchmark data.** The company, people, competitors and every figure in this pack are fictional. They were generated for a reasoning benchmark and are internally consistent, but they are not real market data.

## 1. Context

Brightwork sells field-service management software (scheduling, dispatch, quotes, invoicing) to HVAC,
plumbing and electrical contractors with 3–50 technicians. It has 9,800 customer accounts with an average of
6.2 office seats each (dispatchers and office staff) on the Core plan at $79 per seat per month: annual recurring
revenue (ARR) of $57.6M. Gross margin is 78%, annual logo churn 14%, net revenue retention 101%.

The product team has built **Dispatch Copilot**: AI that proposes a day's schedule, drafts quotes from
technician notes, and summarises customer calls. It ran as a free beta for 12 weeks.

**Decision maker:** CEO Maya Okafor and the executive team, at January 2027 planning.

## 2. Decision question

**Should Brightwork launch Dispatch Copilot in Q2 2027, and if so, how should it be packaged and priced?**

## 3. Objectives and constraints

- Raise net revenue retention from 101% to 105% by 2028.
- Keep company gross margin at or above 75%.
- Engineering: 60 engineers in total. Launching Copilot needs 14 engineers for two quarters, which delays the
  rewrite of the technician mobile app by two quarters.

## 4. Current view inside the company

The Chief Product Officer proposes launching Copilot as a **paid add-on at $149 per account per month**: "Our
survey shows 46% of customers are likely to buy it. That is about $8M of new ARR in the first year."
The Head of Customer Success worries about the mobile app delay: "Mobile reliability is what customers complain
about."

## 5. Beta results (240 accounts, 12 weeks, volunteers)

**Table 1. Beta outcomes**

| Measure | Beta accounts | Matched non-beta accounts |
|---|---|---|
| Self-reported dispatcher hours saved per week | 4.1 | — |
| Change in jobs scheduled per dispatcher-hour vs the prior 12 weeks | +11% | +2% |
| 90-day renewal rate | 97% | 93% |

- Beta accounts volunteered; they are larger (8.1 seats on average) and more active than the base.
- Usage is concentrated: the top 10% of beta accounts generated 58% of all AI requests.

**Table 2. AI requests per account per month (beta)**

|  | Requests per month |
|---|---|
| Median account | 1,900 |
| Mean account | 3,600 |
| Mean of the top 10% of accounts | 14,500 |

- Model inference cost: $0.009 per request under the current provider contract, fixed through December 2027.
  The provider's list prices fell 35% over the past 12 months.
- Running the feature also needs about $0.6M a year of platform, evaluation and support cost.

## 6. Pricing evidence

- **Survey** (October 2026, 610 customer admins): at $149 per account per month, 46% said they were "likely" or
  "very likely" to buy Copilot.
- **Paywall test** (last four weeks of the beta): 120 beta accounts were offered Copilot at $149 per account per
  month after the free period. 17 accounts (14%) bought it. Accounts that bought averaged 6,800 requests a month.
- **Tier option:** a new "Pro" plan that includes Copilot, priced $12 more per seat per month than Core. When
  Brightwork last launched a higher tier (2023), 33% of accounts moved to it within a year.

## 7. Competitor evidence

- **Routewise**, the closest competitor, launched AI scheduling **included in its Pro plan** in September 2026.
- Brightwork's win rate in deals where Routewise competed fell from 44% (Q1–Q2 2026) to 37% (Q3 2026).
  Brightwork has about 2,600 qualified new-customer opportunities a year, and Routewise competes in about 60% of
  them; a new account averages 6.2 seats on Core.
- In Q3 2026 lost deals, 31% of loss notes mention AI features.

## 8. Customer evidence

**Table 3. Main reason given by accounts that churned, 2026 (n = 1,190)**

| Reason | Share |
|---|---|
| Mobile app reliability | 27% |
| Price | 22% |
| Missing integrations | 15% |
| Went out of business / sold | 14% |
| Switched for AI features | 6% |
| Other | 16% |

- Top feature request in the 2026 customer survey: "a reliable technician mobile app" (38% rank it first);
  AI scheduling is ranked first by 19%.

## 9. Costs

- Engineering: 14 engineers for two quarters at a fully loaded $210,000 per engineer-year.

## 10. Other material

- **VP Sales memo:** "31% of our lost deals cite AI, so Copilot would recover about a third of the deals we lose to
  Routewise."
- **Survey method note:** the October survey went to all 9,800 account admins; 610 replied (6%). Respondents average
  9.4 seats, against 6.2 for all accounts.

## 11. Uncertainties

- Whether the productivity gain holds beyond volunteers.
- How fast inference prices fall after 2027.
- Whether Routewise's AI is the cause of the lower win rate or coincides with its price promotion in Q3 2026
  (Routewise also offered 20% off the first year in Q3).

storyline.governing_thought: Launch Dispatch Copilot in Q2 2027 inside a Pro plan at $12 more per seat with a usage allowance, then restart the mobile rewrite

exec_summary.text: Copilot's value is real but demand is overstated: the $8M add-on case earns about $0.8M a year

sub_points.text: Beta jobs per dispatcher-hour rose 11%, against 2% for matched accounts, among volunteers
Only 14% of beta accounts bought at $149; 46% of survey respondents said they would

exec_summary.text: AI must sit inside a plan; Pro at $12 more per seat beats the add-on if it wins twice the accounts

sub_points.text: Recovering the win rate lost to Routewise is worth at most $0.6M of new ARR a year
Pro beats the add-on on ARR, gross profit and payback, but earns half as much per account
At the 2023 tier's 33% uptake, Pro adds about $2.9M of ARR, above the $2.3M the target needs

exec_summary.text: Pro needs a usage allowance, or heavy users would push company margin below the 75% floor

sub_points.text: A top-decile account would cost 1.8 times in inference what an average account pays for Pro
An allowance of 333 requests per seat a month, with paid top-ups, keeps margin above 75%

exec_summary.text: Launch in Q2, then mobile in Q3: Copilot first wins while Pro uptake stays above 25%

sub_points.text: Mobile reliability drives 4.5 times as much churn as missing AI features
Making Pro wait two quarters costs 2.5 percentage points of NRR, against at most 1.9 for mobile
A Q1 test of both offers decides the package: Pro must win twice the add-on's accounts

next_steps.action: Approve the Q2 2027 launch, 14 engineers for Q1–Q2, and Pro at $12 more per seat with a 333-request allowance
Run a randomized two-offer test (Pro and the $149 add-on) with non-beta Core accounts
Confirm that allowance metering and top-up billing fit inside the 14-engineer build
Pull the Q4 2026 win rate against Routewise and track it each quarter
Restart the mobile rewrite at full staffing and open the inference contract renewal

sections.title: Launch in Q2, then mobile, with gates

constraints.item: Company gross margin at or above 75%
constraints.effect: unlimited Copilot breaks it above about 5,300 requests per Pro account; the allowance keeps margin near 77% at full use

constraints.item: 14 of 60 engineers for two quarters, delaying the mobile rewrite by two quarters
constraints.effect: costs up to 1.9 percentage points of NRR; Copilot first wins only above 25% Pro uptake
in the payback row; gross profit figures are before it

constraints.item: $0.6M a year platform, evaluation and support cost
constraints.effect: in every gross profit and margin figure

constraints.item: Inference price fixed at $0.009 through December 2027
constraints.effect: no price fall assumed in 2027; the allowance is revisited at renewal

constraints.item: Allowance metering and top-up billing are not in the 14-engineer estimate
constraints.effect: could lengthen the build or payback; next step asks Engineering to confirm in January

constraints.item: Survey response bias and volunteer beta
constraints.effect: the add-on is sized on the paywall rate and treated as a ceiling

alternatives.why: it meets the NRR target at the measured 14% rate and earns twice as much per account; Pro wins only if it converts twice as many accounts, so the add-on is the fallback at the first gate

alternatives.option: Mobile rewrite first, Copilot two quarters later
alternatives.why: costs 2.5 percentage points of NRR against at most 1.9 for Copilot first at base uptake; flips below 25% uptake, which the Q1 test checks
heavy users cost more than they pay and margin falls below 75% above about 5,300 requests per account

failure_threshold.driver: share of accounts moving to Pro
failure_threshold.threshold: below about 25% Pro uptake, mobile first is better; below 26% the NRR target is missed; Pro must convert twice the add-on's accounts to match its ARR
failure_threshold.range: Pro ARR low $1.22M (14%) / base $2.89M (33%); no evidence for a high case

consistency.headline: Launch Dispatch Copilot in Q2 2027 inside a Pro plan at $12 more per seat with a usage allowance, then restart the mobile rewrite
consistency.fix: the packaging claim is conditioned on Pro winning twice as many accounts as the add-on (exec item 2, slide 5 title) and backed by the first gate

cases.base: Pro at 33% uptake: $2.89M ARR, 5.0 percentage points of NRR, gross profit at least $1.57M, margin 76.9%
cases.stress: Pro at 14% uptake: $1.22M ARR, 2.1 percentage points of NRR, gross profit $0.32M, margin 76.9%; misses the NRR target and mobile first becomes better

gates.metric: Pro conversion compared with add-on conversion in a randomized two-offer test
gates.response: launch the $149 add-on in Q2 instead of Pro

gates.metric: win rate against Routewise in Q4 2026
gates.response: treat the Q3 fall as price-driven and drop win-back from the case

gates.metric: share of accounts on Pro six months after launch
gates.response: offer the add-on to Core accounts alongside Pro

gates.threshold: rewrite delayed by more than 2 quarters in total
